$comment: APPEND-ONLY wire-ABI ledger for herdr-mx. One entry per (protocol_version, wire_abi_epoch) this fork has shipped, oldest first. Hand-maintained; checked by `abi_history_*` in src/protocol/wire_fixtures.rs. Adding an entry is the ONLY correct response to a red `wire_schema_fingerprint_is_pinned` — repinning the constant without appending here is the laundering the whole mechanism exists to prevent.
rules: 1. Existing fixture corpora are never overwritten. Only the LAST entry may point at docs/next/protocol/fixtures.json (the live, regenerated corpus); every earlier entry must point at a file under docs/next/protocol/fixtures/ whose sha256 is pinned here.

2. A wire change bumps WIRE_ABI_EPOCH (src/protocol/abi.rs), repins WIRE_SCHEMA_FINGERPRINT, archives the outgoing fixtures.json under fixtures/, and appends an entry here. `fixtures_are_current` then forces the new corpus to be regenerated.

3. Every entry states, explicitly, whether the current server still accepts that ABI. `accepted_by_current_server: true` MUST have a matching row in `abi::accepted_wire_abis()`; the two are compared by `abi_history_mirrors_the_accepted_table`. Silence is not a decision.

entries.decision: REJECTED. Epoch 0 is the pre-prelude handshake: it announced no fork, no epoch and no schema fingerprint, so a peer speaking it cannot be identified at all. An unannotated Hello claiming protocol 20 is equally consistent with herdr-mx and with upstream/master, and those two disagree on ClientLaunchMode::TerminalAttach (1 vs 2) and ServerMessage::Terminal (13 vs 2) - mobile/.prd/03-blockers.md B1. Accepting epoch 0 would therefore mean guessing, and a wrong guess is a silent mis-parse rather than a loud rejection, which is exactly the failure M0-a was created to remove. Note the fingerprint field is null on purpose: epoch 0 builds never computed one, so recording a value here would be a claim about bytes nobody ever sent.
entries.user_impact: A herdr client built before this change cannot connect to a server built after it, and vice versa. This is the same breakage class as any PROTOCOL_VERSION bump (11 of them in the 79 days to 2026-08-08), and it lands on the same, already-built recovery path: `validate_running_server_compatibility` (src/server/autodetect.rs) compares the running server's reported protocol before a socket is even opened and prints the session restart guidance. Rejection is also diagnosable on the socket itself - the server answers a prelude-less client with a legacy-framed Welcome carrying `abi::legacy_peer_rejection()`, so an old client prints a reason instead of dying on an unexplained close.

entries.decision: REJECTED, and the reason is asymmetry rather than ambiguity - unlike epoch 0, an epoch-1 peer identifies itself perfectly. Epoch 2 only APPENDS ClientMessage::RetargetTerminal at tag 14, so an epoch-1 client talking to this server is genuinely safe: it never emits tag 14 and every ServerMessage is byte-identical. The reverse is not. An epoch-2 client (the mobile app is the whole reason this axis exists) sends RetargetTerminal on its first pane swipe, and an epoch-1 server has no tag 14 - it fails the bincode decode and drops the connection. Since check_peer_abi is the same table on both ends, accepting epoch 1 here would accept it in BOTH directions and buy a working old-client/new-server pair at the price of a new-client/old-server pair that dies on the first swipe instead of refusing to connect. There is no capability negotiation in Welcome to split the two, so the honest window is the empty one. Second, smaller reason: epoch 1 was introduced earlier the same day on this same unmerged branch and never shipped, so accepting it would be declaring support for a peer that does not exist anywhere.
entries.user_impact: No user is affected: no epoch-1 build was ever released. If one is built from an intermediate commit of feat/mobile-client, it is refused on the prelude with the axis named ('incompatible wire ABI epoch: peer ... vs this build ...', src/protocol/abi.rs check_peer_abi), which is a diagnosable refusal rather than a mis-parse, and the existing pre-connection check (validate_running_server_compatibility, src/server/autodetect.rs) still prints the session restart guidance before a socket is opened.

entries.decision: REJECTED, for the same asymmetry reason epoch 1 was: epoch 3 only APPENDS to the message set, so an epoch-2 client is genuinely safe against an epoch-3 server, but an epoch-3 client is not safe against an epoch-2 server - it may emit ClientMessage::GraphicsTransmissionResult (tag 15), InputPixels (16) or GraphicsTransmissionStarted (17), and an epoch-2 server has no such tags and drops the connection on the bincode decode. check_peer_abi is one table used in both directions, so accepting epoch 2 would buy the safe direction at the price of the unsafe one. Epoch 3 also CHANGES an existing payload - MouseCapture gained a trailing sgr_pixels: bool (upstream v0.8.2). The effect of that is frame-local, not stream-wide, and it is worth stating exactly because the loose version ('desync', 'silent mis-parse') is wrong on this wire: every message carries a 4-byte LE length prefix (write_message, src/protocol/wire.rs:1247-1248), so the next frame's offset is always known and a payload-size change cannot desynchronize the stream. On the uncompressed path, read_message enforces that the decoder consumed the whole payload (src/protocol/wire.rs:1284-1290, `consumed != claimed_len` -> FramingError::Bincode), so an epoch-2 client fed an epoch-3 MouseCapture gets a LOUD per-frame error, not a quiet one. Only the compressed path is quiet: decompress_server_message discards the consumed count (src/protocol/wire.rs:1229-1230, `Ok((inner, _)) => inner`) and has no trailing guard, so the extra byte is dropped silently - and because sgr_pixels is the LAST field, `enabled` still decodes correctly, making that case harmless field loss rather than a mis-parse. So this payload change is a supporting reason to keep the window empty, not the load-bearing one; the tag-15/16/17 argument above stands on its own. Second, smaller reason: epoch 2 was introduced earlier the same day on this same unmerged branch and never shipped.
entries.user_impact: No user is affected: no epoch-2 build was ever released. A build made from an intermediate commit of feat/mobile-client is refused on the prelude with the axis named ('incompatible wire ABI epoch', src/protocol/abi.rs check_peer_abi), and the existing pre-connection check (validate_running_server_compatibility, src/server/autodetect.rs) still prints the session restart guidance before a socket is opened.

entries.decision: ACCEPTED - this is the ABI this build speaks. Epoch 3 is the upstream v0.8.2 merge (133 commits, v0.8.0..v0.8.2). Upstream appended three ClientMessage variants (GraphicsTransmissionResult, InputPixels, GraphicsTransmissionStarted) and three ServerMessage variants (TerminalBell, GraphicsFile, GraphicsTransmissionRetired) at ITS enum tails, and inserted ClientLaunchMode::AppDirectGraphics between App and TerminalAttach; this fork moved AppDirectGraphics to the tail and placed upstream's six new variants after the mx variants, per the standing tail rule. Independent witness that the rule held: the `enums` block of docs/next/protocol/fixtures.json is byte-identical across the merge (ServerMessage::Terminal 13, ClientMessage::ObserveTerminal 12, RetargetTerminal 14, ClientLaunchMode::TerminalAttach 1), and client_message_wire_tags_preserve_protocol_15_order / server_message_wire_tags_preserve_protocol_20_order still pin every pre-existing tag. What DID change, and why the fingerprint had to move: the message set grew, and ServerMessage::MouseCapture gained a trailing sgr_pixels: bool (a payload change at an unmoved tag - the exact case fingerprint_changes_when_a_payload_field_is_added exists for). PROTOCOL_VERSION deliberately stays at 21: the handshake byte stream (28-byte prelude, Hello, Welcome) is unchanged, upstream is still on 20, and the version names the negotiation while the epoch names the byte layout.
entries.user_impact: For a client and server from this build, nothing changes: the desktop TUI, herdr attach, the observe/terminal-ANSI stream and the JSON API all still put the same bytes on the wire for every message that existed before the merge. One observable change is not an ABI change but a size change, and it lands on the mobile observe path: upstream's 'compact large terminal redraws' (#2675, 36074530) rewrote write_all_cells (src/protocol/render_ansi.rs:639) to elide the per-cell cursor move when the next cell is inline and to re-emit SGR only when the style actually changes. That function is not fixture-only - it is the single encoder on the live observe path: src/server/render_stream.rs:101 (PreparedRender::TerminalAnsi) calls BlitEncoder::encode, whose full-redraw arm is src/protocol/render_ansi.rs:483 write_all_cells, and the bytes it returns become ServerMessage::Terminal verbatim (src/server/render_stream.rs:114-121). Measured at 100x30 on this tree AFTER the merge: 3,276 bytes live (tests/observe_terminal_ansi.rs, 2 consecutive runs) and 3,274 from the TypeScript client over both a direct socket and the ssh bridge, against 3,292 for the synthesized fixture; the pre-merge numbers were 55,925 live and 55,921 in the fixture. So a full frame on the phone is ~17x cheaper, which retires the 'marshal a ~56 KB frame across the React Native bridge' cost that mobile/.prd/03-blockers.md B13 was written against - that blocker's measurements are now stale and its mitigation (reduce full-frame FREQUENCY via RetargetTerminal) is no longer load-bearing for size alone. A client built at epoch 2 or earlier cannot connect to this server and vice versa; that refusal is the epoch-2 row above and lands on the same already-built recovery path as any PROTOCOL_VERSION bump.
